synopsis: An ordinary commute ascends beyond the clouds and crosses a celestial bridge made of pure light, spanning a cosmic void where gods' fortresses gleam.

shots.prompt:
HOOK. Open already mid-motion on a dull ordinary commute, one everyday object streaking past the glass at arm's length. At about 1.2 seconds a two-note chime cuts in and a calm neutral announcer says the destination line; nobody reacts. The train slams into acceleration. THE ORDINARY WORLD LASTS AT MOST 2.5 SECONDS. At about 2.5 seconds the first total cover wipes the pane and the glass clears further down the same line, where ONE thing in the distance is unmistakably wrong and already growing. At about 5.0 seconds a harder cover wipes it again: the wrong thing now owns a third of the horizon and the passengers turn their heads to the glass. At about 7.5 seconds a third cover clears onto the threshold itself, close and unavoidable, the line committed. Every cover is a blow that throws the passengers. PASSENGER PHYSICS ON THE CLOCK: in the SAME frames as each cover time above, and not before or after it, the standing passengers are visibly thrown, swing hard on the poles, stumble a step, snatch at a strap and cry out; on the hardest cover a body is flung far enough to break its silhouette against the glass. If a cover lands and no body moves, the shot is wrong. Remember the canon: the camera never moves from its one fixed place, looking out SIDEWAYS through the left glass wall that curves up into a glass roof, with the standing passengers gripping poles along the right edge; the world only ever streaks ACROSS the glass and never toward the camera; the view changes only behind an opaque environmental cover lasting about a fifth of a second; and no second of this shot is ever a still frame.
